title: A product of factorized base centres dominates local module flatifications
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, $U\subset S$ a quasi-compact open, $f:X\to S$ a morphism of schemes, and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Let $R$ be a finite index set. For each $r\in R$ let $T_r$ be a qcqs scheme and let $g_r:Y_r\to T_r$, $e_r:T_r\to S$ and $j_r:Y_r\to X$ satisfy $e_r g_r=fj_r$. Assume $e_r$ is quasi-compact and flat, and $j_r$ is flat. Let $\mathcal J_r,\mathcal J'_r\subset\mathcal O_{T_r}$ and $\mathcal I_r\subset\mathcal O_S$ be finite-type quasi-coherent ideals such that $\mathcal I_r|_U=\mathcal O_U$ and
$$\mathcal I_r\mathcal O_{T_r}=\mathcal J_r\mathcal J'_r.$$
Assume the strict transform of $j_r^*\mathcal F$ for $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_r}T_r\to T_r$ is flat over that blowup. Define
$$\mathcal I=\prod_{r\in R}\mathcal I_r,\qquad b:S^b=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}S\to S,$$
using the unit ideal for an empty product. Then $\mathcal I$ is finite type and $V(\mathcal I)=\bigcup_rV(\mathcal I_r)\subset S\setminus U$, so $b$ is $U$-admissible. For each $r$, put
$$\mathcal K_r=\mathcal J'_r\prod_{t\ne r}(\mathcal I_t\mathcal O_{T_r}),\qquad T_r^b=T_r\times_SS^b.$$
There are canonical isomorphisms over $T_r$
$$T_r^b\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_r\mathcal K_r}T_r\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K_r\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_r}T_r}}(\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_r}T_r).$$
Writing $c_r:\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_r}T_r\to T_r$, the support of the product centre equals
$$V(\mathcal J_r\mathcal K_r)=V(\mathcal J_r)\cup c_r\bigl(V(\mathcal K_r\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_r}T_r})\bigr).$$
On $Y_r\times_SS^b=Y_r\times_{T_r}T_r^b$, the pullback of $\mathcal F^b$ is canonically the successive strict transform of $j_r^*\mathcal F$ along the two blowups in the display, compatibly with the ordinary-pullback quotient maps. It is the ordinary pullback of the first, flat strict transform along the second blowup and is flat over $T_r^b$. Schemes, qcqs conventions, quasi-coherence, relative module flatness, admissible blowups, module strict transforms, fibre products and module pullbacks are as in [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], [def-trf-module-strict-transform], [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-pc-module-pullback]. Flat morphisms are as in [def-weil-flat-morphism], and $V$ denotes the underlying zero set of an ideal. Blowups themselves are those of [def-nagata-global-blowup].

proof.text: Products of quasi-coherent ideals are quasi-coherent: express a binary product as the image of the multiplication map from the tensor product, and apply the cited tensor and image statements. On an affine open where the factors have finite generating sets, their pairwise products generate the product ideal; induction gives finite type for a finite product. Extension of an ideal is the image of its module pullback, by the cited closed-subscheme base-change statement and the definition of extended ideal. Thus on affine opens its generators are the images of the original generators; extension preserves finite type and finite products. These observations apply to $\mathcal I$, to each $\mathcal K_r$, and to its extension to $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_r}T_r$. At a point a finite product of ideals of the local ring is the unit ideal exactly when every factor is the unit ideal (the product is contained in each factor). Therefore $V(\mathcal I)=\bigcup_r V(\mathcal I_r)$, and $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$. The defining datum makes $b$ $U$-admissible. For $R=\varnothing$ the ideal is $\mathcal O_S$ and there are no assertions indexed by $r$.

source.place: Tag 0814, lemma-flatten-module-etale-localize, proof paragraph 2: finite product of base ideals

proof.text: Fix $r$ and abbreviate $T=T_r$, $Y=Y_r$, $J=\mathcal J_r$, $K=\mathcal K_r$. Extension and multiplication as in Step 1 give $\mathcal I\mathcal O_T=(\mathcal I_r\mathcal O_T)\prod_{t\ne r}(\mathcal I_t\mathcal O_T)=JK$. Since $e_r$ is flat, the specified flat base-change comparison identifies $T_r^b=T\times_SS^b$ with $\operatorname{Bl}_{JK}T$. Apply the product-ideal comparison to $J,K$: its two constructed maps are inverse, so this is also the blowup of $K\mathcal O_{T_1}$ on $T_1=\operatorname{Bl}_JT$. Write $c:T_1\to T$ and $d:T_2\to T_1$ for these two blowups. Both identifications are over $T$.

The product criterion in local rings gives $V(JK)=V(J)\cup V(K)$. The underlying zero set of the extended ideal $K\mathcal O_{T_1}$ is $c^{-1}V(K)$, since the closed subscheme defined by the extension is its fibre product. Thus its image under $c$ is contained in $V(K)$. Conversely, if $t\in V(K)\setminus V(J)$, the complement isomorphism for the $J$-blowup supplies its unique preimage in $T_1$, which lies in $c^{-1}V(K)$. Points in $V(J)$ are already in the first summand. This proves $V(JK)=V(J)\cup c(V(K\mathcal O_{T_1}))$. This argument does not assert that $c$ is surjective over $V(J)$.

Put $M=j_r^*\mathcal F$, which is quasi-coherent by pullback. Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be its successive module strict transforms along $c,d$, and $G$ its strict transform along the specified $JK$-blowup. Apply the comparison-epimorphism statement with base $T$, ideals $J$, $K\mathcal O_{T_1}$ and total centre $JK$. Step 2 supplies the required isomorphism of the composite blowup, and Step 3 supplies exactly the required support equality. It gives an epimorphism $\theta:M_2\twoheadrightarrow G$ commuting with the composite quotient from the ordinary pullback; every local section of its kernel is supported on the inverse image of $V(JK)$.

Apply the iterated-transform exceptional-support statement to the same $c,d,M$. It says $M_2$ has no nonzero local sections supported on the inverse image of $V(K\mathcal O_{T_1})\cup c^{-1}V(J)$, and identifies that inverse image with the inverse image of $V(J)\cup c(V(K\mathcal O_{T_1}))$. By Step 3 this is exactly the support allowed for $\ker\theta$ in Step 4. Hence the kernel is zero. Since $\theta$ is already surjective, it is the canonical isomorphism $M_2\cong G$. The identity $\theta\alpha=\beta$ in Step 4 proves compatibility with the ordinary-pullback quotient maps, not just an abstract isomorphism.

Use the flat-pullback comparison of module strict transforms for the original commuting square $(f,e_r,g_r,j_r)$ and the finite-type ideal $\mathcal I$. Its hypotheses are precisely the assumed flatness of both $e_r$ and $j_r$, and the quasi-coherence of $\mathcal F$. It identifies the pullback of $\mathcal F^b$ on $Y\times_T T_r^b$ with $G$, compatibly with the ordinary-pullback quotient maps. The fibre-product universal property identifies $Y\times_T(T\times_SS^b)$ with $Y\times_SS^b$ by the maps to $Y$ and $S^b$. Combining this comparison with Step 5 gives the asserted successive transform on the stated scheme, with its quotient compatibility.

proof.text: By hypothesis $M_1$ is flat over $T_1$. Its ordinary pullback $N$ to $Y\times_T T_2$ is flat over $T_2$ by relative-flat-module pullback, without any flatness requirement on $d$. The extended centre $(K\mathcal O_{T_1})\mathcal O_{T_2}$ defines an effective Cartier divisor by principalization of the blowup centre. Apply relative-flat Cartier-support vanishing to $N$: it has no nonzero local sections supported on the inverse image of that divisor. The strict-transform sheaf-kernel statement identifies the defining kernel of $N\twoheadrightarrow M_2$ with precisely these sections, so this kernel is zero and the defining quotient is an isomorphism. Consequently $M_2=N$ is the ordinary pullback of the first flat strict transform and is flat over $T_2=T_r^b$. Together with Step 6 this proves the remaining assertions.
